entry.title: Why I Switched from ChromaDB to ElasticSearch (and What I Miss)
entry.summary: My AI system had been extracting knowledge from emails for weeks. Thousands of facts, entities, patterns, all sitting in PostgreSQL. The problem was finding any of it. The brain was using hardcoded SQL filters like WHERE category = 'infrastructure' to pull context before making decisions. If a fact about hosting costs was categorized under "billing," the brain would never see it when reasoning about infrastructure. I needed to search by meaning, not by label. But I also needed to search by exact match. An invoice number like "TDS-2026-003" has no semantic meaning. You can't find it with vector search. entry.title: Architecture Philosophy: Rule-First Design
entry.summary:
The Core Question
When building an engine to verify AI-written code, architects hit a brutal dilemma. Where do rules live, and who enforces them? Axiom's answer is simple. Rules must precede code. Traditional software development works like this: Write code first. Run tests to catch bugs. Add rules to prevent similar bugs. Repeat forever. This reactive approach shatters catastrophically when verifying AI-generated code. LLMs excel at crafting outputs that pass tests while concealing logical flaws—they're geniuses at creating "plausible wrong answers." Their probabilistic nature means bugs reappear in subtly different forms, bypassing test-based detection. Without rules locked in first, the engine eventually gaslights itself. It starts lowering verification standards to accommodate AI hal…
